title: Choose the Rider-led cw-code design
question: The T3 structure is fixed. These vary only the visual system and the Rider/VS Code balance. Choose one, or tell me which details to combine.

options.label: Rider Graphite
options.lineage: Rider surface depth with T3 hierarchy
options.thesis: A quiet Rider interpretation: stepped graphite work surfaces, compact IDE controls, and precise cyan focus without changing the current shell.
options.viewport: The current three-region shell remains intact. Narrow gutters and tonal steps create pane depth; the right workspace is open to Diff.
options.risk: Its restraint may still feel conservative if cw-code needs a more recognizable accent signature.

options.label: Rider Teal Studio
options.lineage: Rider New UI chrome and panels with T3 session composition
options.thesis: A smoky teal titlebar, clearly layered inset panes, cyan focus, and violet tooling accents give cw-code a stronger native IDE identity.
options.viewport: The same sidebar, thread, and contextual workspace sit inside a Rider-like app ground with soft outer rounding and narrow gutters.
options.risk: The colored titlebar and brighter accents are more distinctive and need careful restraint during implementation.

options.label: Rider Violet Workbench
options.lineage: Rider’s chromatic syntax and tabs with VS Code docking density
options.thesis: A graphite-violet workspace gives active context more personality while the expanded Diff and Terminal area demonstrates serious tooling density.
options.viewport: The existing right workspace expands and splits internally between Diff and Terminal; the project/session and conversation regions remain unchanged.
options.risk: The violet signature is memorable but could become visually loud if repeated beyond active context and tooling.
